P01.note: Most tempting is C (Verrow vs Tenlow, same season), but both lack gas so it bears only on Vasquez. The key itself is confounded: Tenlow's late exchange could explain its later dinners, so D weakens Tennant only partially; the cleaner Verrow-later-than-Sudmere comparison is absent.

P02.note: A is tempting (Aldmoss thinned more than Dellow) but carries both factors. C is the rival's clean test and D reverses dredging, both strikable as pointing the wrong way.
P02.not_hard_because: Aldmoss and Cadfield are described in one sentence as differing only in dredging ('receives just as much of the discharge'), which hands over the controlled pair.

P03.note: C (Galmby vs Ilvard) is tempting but the lakeshore city also has pavement heat. A pits a lake village against an inland city, so the lake effect wins against the rival's factor; a student looking for the 'matched' pair (city vs city) will not find it.

P04.note: A (Ardvane, 0.75) is the highest ratio but a rat-free island, struck by the Rats column on sight. C (0.578) and B (0.55) are near misses below 0.6.
P04.not_hard_because: Only one division per option and the rats column removes the most tempting option immediately; three yes-rats rows, one clears 0.6.

P05.note: D and B are tempting but straddle the war decade; A actually supports Vollmer. C is a within-town before/after comparison across two peacetime decades, which most students will not look for first.

P06.note: B is tempting (6 km beats 12 km) but Orrinby is hilly. The key A is confounded by Nettleford's stations, and the clean Pellam-vs-Mossgate test is absent, so the student must accept a rival-factor comparison.

P07.note: C (Uxley, 30%) is the highest share but charged admission, struck on sight. B (Yoxholt 24.5%) is the near miss.
P07.not_hard_because: One division per free row; the charged row is the only one above a quarter besides the key, so the Admission column does most of the work.

P08.note: D is the trap: Quorley fell from 2015 to 2020, but spending was falling everywhere anyway. A and C bear on the campaign. B compares the tax-only town with the untouched neighbour, though only in 2020 levels.

P09.note: A (Sarnby vs Yarnholt) is tempting but Sarnby has both factors. B reverses installment, C is the rival's test.
P09.not_hard_because: The passage sentence 'of those two towns, only Sarnby also had a conservatory' sets up the Sarnby/Ulmeston controlled pair; same 2x2 template as P02 and P20.

P10.note: B (Prestley) is tempting: 84% completion but only a $3.90 gain. A (Orwen) fails both. Options show only wages, so completion must be read from the table.
P10.not_hard_because: Two-condition filter with only one row passing both; the same template as P30, and Orwen's $3.55 gain is visibly short.

P11.note: A is same-season but reversed. B and C mix seasons and are struck on sight because both historians accept winter worsens haze.
P11.not_hard_because: Mixed-season options are dead on arrival, leaving a same-season pair where one is reversed; same template as P01, P12, P21, P25, P28, P32.

P12.note: B (Norrance vs Mellick weekends) is same-day but points against the charge. A and C mix weekdays and weekends.
P12.not_hard_because: Mixed weekday/weekend options are struck on sight; the weekday pair Mellick vs Pasterby differs only in the charge, as the passage's 'like Mellick' signposts.

P13.note: B is tempting but supports fencing (and confounds burning's end). D supports burning without bearing on fences. A pits burned-unfenced against fenced in the same decade.

P14.note: C (Kolbeck 6.3 vs Hennick 3.5) is the trap at 1.8x. A has both inside; B has the inner asteroid higher, reversed.
P14.not_hard_because: Distance column against 2.7 strikes two options at once; only a single ratio check separates C from D.

P15.note: D tempts but Cromby is upland. B supports pesticide, C reverses mites. A pits heavy mites against light mites plus pesticide, both lowland.

P16.note: D tempts as a cross-line pair but runs the wrong way (inside outsells outside). B and C do not straddle the line in the claimed direction.
P16.not_hard_because: Only one option has the farther station outside the line and the nearer inside with the farther selling more; read off the distance column.

P17.note: A (Ulvercote, 1.87x) and C (Varrick, 1.7x) are tempting large gains; D (Tavisholm, 2.35x) more than doubled but has 610 seats. Options quote only the 1900 figure, forcing a 1890 lookup and a ratio.

P18.note: C tempts but uses Ruskett's large farms, which adopt early anyway. A supports Okoro; D is the rival's test.
P18.not_hard_because: The passage flags farm size and Ruskett's estates, so every 'large farms' option is dead; the small-vs-small pair with the no-office village winning is the key.

P19.note: A is the only cross-threshold distractor and runs the wrong way. C has both sites below 1.1 m, D both above.
P19.not_hard_because: Height column against 1.1 m strikes two options instantly; of the two straddling options, only one has the higher site more crowded, readable directly.

P20.note: B (Morwen vs Quellin) is tempting but Morwen has both features. A supports Nakagawa, D runs against porches.
P20.not_hard_because: 2x2 template identical to P02 and P09: the single-factor pair (porch, through street vs none) is the key.

P21.note: A tempts (Esterholm earlier) but Esterholm has oaks too. D mixes springs, B reverses feeders.
P21.not_hard_because: Mixed-spring option struck on sight; Coppling vs Dinsmore are explicitly both beech, differing only in feeders.

P22.note: A tempts (Lanner rose) but Lanner has logging too. D uses the wet year 2012. C reverses the gravel effect. B pits gravel-only Holt against logging-only Kell in two dry post-2010 years, requiring the student to track four dated conditions.

P23.note: B tempts but Gessing has a sheet; A supports both factors; D uses high Kaltby.
P23.not_hard_because: Ilmer and Holvard share elevation and lack a sheet, so a thinner layer losing less directly refutes; passage signposts 'only Gessing adds a sheet'.

P24.note: B (Ollerby, 3.6) clears the bar but has a college, struck on sight. D (2.94) is the near miss.
P24.not_hard_because: Same template as P04, P07, P26, P27: the highest-ratio row is excluded by the category column, leaving one division per option.

P25.note: C (Ulverholm wet vs Sallowby wet) is same-condition but reversed. B and D mix dry and wet years.
P25.not_hard_because: Mixed dry/wet options struck on sight; the remaining same-year pair where the fire-company town wins is the key; same seasonal template as P11 and P32.

P26.note: A (Haverud, 2,053 per MW) is highest but tracking, struck by the mounting column. B (Islaug, 1,679) is the near miss just below 1,700.
P26.not_hard_because: Category column removes the top-ratio option; one division per fixed row decides it; same template as P04, P07, P24, P27.

P27.note: B (Lauvholm, 18%) clears 15% but has groynes. C (Hestrand, 12%) is the near miss with the largest absolute gain, which tempts students who read meters not percent.
P27.not_hard_because: Groynes column strikes the only other qualifying row; Hestrand's 11 m gain is the only real trap.

P28.note: C tempts as a same-month comparison but bears on logging. A supports Brevard. D pits logged-no-worms against worms-unlogged in the same month.

P29.note: A (Vintrell vs Wrayburn brides) tempts as 40 vs 15 years but Vintrell is on the turnpike. B and D compare grooms with brides. C has the schoolmaster parish winning despite lacking the road.

P30.note: A (Birchtop, 7-point drop) is tempting but takes 78 days, a column the options never quote. B and D drop more than 10 points.
P30.not_hard_because: Two-condition filter like P10; the tempting option fails on the unquoted column, the same trick used there.

P31.note: C (Sedgeholm, 1 per 1,300) is the densest trade but 61% literacy. D (Wickerby, 38%) and A (Ulsworth) fail on 1,800 and 1,720. Options quote only bookshops, forcing two more column lookups and a division.

P32.note: C is same-season but supports turbines. A and D mix winter and summer.
P32.not_hard_because: Mixed-season options struck on sight given the stated storm effect; same template as P01, P11, P12, P21, P25, P28.

tells: On every item with a stated nuisance factor (season, weekday/weekend, dry/wet year, decade, groom/bride), options that mix the two levels of that factor are never the key; striking them leaves two matched-condition options, one of which points the wrong way: P01, P05, P11, P12, P13, P21, P22, P25, P28, P29, P32.

On hypothesis items the key's 'winning' location has the hypothesized factor and lacks the rival's (or the losing location has only the rival's factor); options where the winner has both factors are always distractors: P01, P03, P06, P11, P13, P15, P18, P22, P25, P28, P29, P32.
On the four-location 2x2 items the key is always the pair the passage signposts as differing in one factor only ('just as much', 'only Sarnby also', 'like Mellick'): P02, P09, P12, P20, P21, P23.
On threshold-ratio table items the highest-ratio row is always excluded by the yes/no category column, and the key is the only in-category row just over the bar: P04, P07, P24, P26, P27, P31.
On two-condition filter items the most tempting distractor passes the quoted condition and fails on the column the options never quote: P10, P17, P30, P31.
near_duplicates: two hypotheses, three or four locations, one shared seasonal confound, same option shape
2x2 factorial towns, key is the single-factor controlled pair
ratio threshold with a category column excluding the top row
two-condition filter where only one row passes both
pairs straddling a numeric cutoff, one cross-cutoff option in the right direction
time-series factor onset with a confounding period, within-site or cross-site decade comparison
options quote one cell and the key needs further columns plus a ratio
